W7221094773.title: Pt/MnOx/C Catalysts from Electrolytic Manganese Residue and Oil Sludge for VUV Photocatalytic CO Oxidation: Synergistic Bio-Pretreatment and Polyphenol-Mediated Pt Dispersion
W7221094773.abstract: The valorization of hazardous industrial wastes into high-performance catalytic materials presents a compelling route to address both environmental pollution and resource scarcity. This work presents a closed-loop strategy for the fabrication of Pt/MnOx/C composite catalysts using electrolytic manganese residue and oil sludge. The strategy integrates anaerobic co-fermentation with mixed halophilic desulfurizing bacteria and polyphenol-mediated Pt dispersion via blueberry extract. The optimal catalyst achieves an exceptional vacuum ultraviolet photocatalytic carbon monoxide oxidation efficiency of 97.79% at ambient temperature, with an endpoint-derived apparent pseudo-first-order rate constant of 0.128 min−1, outperforming a commercial Pt/Al2O3 reference (2.5 wt% Pt) by a factor of 4.4 in apparent rate constant (equivalent to 1.7-fold in 30 min conversion efficiency) while utilizing less than half the noble metal loading (1.12 wt% Pt). Comprehensive characterization reveals a genuine structural synergy arising from (i) ultrafine Pt0 nanoparticles (2.1 nm) anchored at MnOx–carbon interfaces, (ii) a mixed-valence MnOx matrix (Mn2+/Mn3+ = 1.8:1) with abundant surface oxygen defects (28.3% of the O 1s envelope, an upper bound corroborated by EPR spectroscopy) for reactive oxygen species trapping, and (iii) Nitrogen-doped carbon domains (2.8 atomic percent) that facilitate electron transfer. In situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier-transform spectroscopy and kinetic analyses are consistent with a Langmuir–Hinshelwood-type mechanism, where CO is activated on Pt0 and reacts with O2 dissociated at oxygen vacancies under vacuum ultraviolet excitation. This work establishes a sustainable paradigm for transforming industrial wastes into high-value photocatalysts, offering a viable pathway toward low-temperature air purification and circular resource utilization.

W7213874267.title: A novel simulated self-solar-tracking photocatalytic device driven by NiTi shape memory alloy with VOC conversion under variable light incidence and controlled indoor conditions

W7214398814.title: P–N Junction-Based Photocatalysts: Synthesis, Mechanism, and Their Applications
W7214398814.abstract: Abstract P–N junction photocatalysts have emerged as versatile and efficient semiconductor materials for solar-driven environmental and energy applications due to their intrinsic ability to promote directional charge separation via a built-in electric field. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the fundamental principles governing P–N junction formation, including band alignment, Fermi-level equilibration, and interfacial charge-transfer mechanisms, and correlates these features with photocatalytic performance. Particular emphasis is placed on the role of the internal electric field in suppressing electron–hole pair recombination and enabling spatial separation of redox reactions. The applications of P–N junction photocatalysts are systematically discussed across environmental pollutant remediation, energy conversion, air purification, and antibacterial activity. In pollutant degradation systems, P–N systems exhibit dual degradation mechanisms, employing an electron-driven reduction process for heavy-metal removal and reactive-oxygen-species-mediated oxidation pathways for the degradation of nonheavy-metal pollutants, such as dyes, pharmaceuticals, and pesticides. For energy applications, the review examines photocatalytic hydrogen (H2) evolution and CO2 reduction, emphasizing the importance of band structure engineering and multielectron transfer pathways in determining activity and product selectivity. Air purification and antimicrobial applications further demonstrate the effectiveness of P–N junctions in generating sustained oxidative species for degradation of gaseous pollutants and pathogen inactivation. A comparative mechanistic framework is presented to unify these diverse applications, illustrating how charge-carrier dynamics dictate reaction pathways. Finally, key challenges, including interfacial control, stability, and scalability, are critically evaluated, and future research directions focusing on advanced material design, in situ characterization, field implementation of P–N junction photocatalysts, and their potential application in sustainable environmental and energy technologies are proposed.

W7221085863.title: Architectural modulation of TiO2 nanostructures for light-assisted regeneration of VOC adsorbents

W7213454782.title: A Z-scheme WO₃–ZnO–TiO₂ nanocomposite coated filter for concurrent PM2.5 filtration and toluene photomineralization under visible light
W7213454782.abstract: Indoor air quality is increasingly compromised by particulate matter (PM) and volatile organic compounds (VOCs), posing compounded health risks in enclosed environments. Conventional purification technologies typically address these pollutants independently, relying on energy-intensive filtration or saturation-limited adsorption. Herein, a dual-functional air purification medium is developed by immobilizing a ternary WO₃–ZnO–TiO₂ nanocomposite onto porous borosilicate glass fibers via a scalable sol–gel dip-coating method. Structural and optical characterization (X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM–EDS), and ultraviolet–visible diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (UV–Vis DRS)) confirms a well-coupled heterojunction with a reduced bandgap of 2.82 eV, enabling photoactivation under visible light (λ > 420 nm). Aerodynamic evaluation demonstrates that hierarchical surface roughness enhances the capture efficiency of 0.3 μm particles from ~ 45% to > 95%, with only a modest pressure drop increase (~ 25 Pa at 1.0 m s⁻¹). Photocatalytic testing using gaseous toluene (50 ppm) reveals > 90% degradation within 90 min under visible light, with an apparent rate constant (k_app) of 0.035 min⁻¹—seven times higher than pristine TiO₂. Carbon dioxide evolution indicates ~ 68% mineralization of degraded toluene. Importantly, the functionalized filter retains ~ 85% VOC removal efficiency under heavy particulate loading (300 µg m⁻³) and maintains ~ 90% activity over twelve consecutive cycles (24 h total runtime). These findings establish the WO₃–ZnO–TiO₂ coated filter as a mechanically robust, energy-efficient platform for simultaneous mitigation of particulate and gaseous indoor pollutants.

W7216498780.title: Atomic-scale synergistic dipole engineering of terminal and bridging hydroxyls for VOC photocatalytic degradation over Sr2Sb2O7

W7213339260.title: RARE-EARTH METAL-DOPED CATALYSTS FOR VOLATILE ORGANIC COMPOUND OXIDATION: MECHANISMS, STRUCTURE–ACTIVITY RELATIONSHIPS, AND FUTURE DIRECTIONS
W7213339260.journal: International Journal of Science and Research Archive
W7213339260.abstract: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are important atmospheric and indoor pollutants because they participate in photochemical ozone and secondary aerosol formation and include compounds with substantial toxicity. Catalytic oxidation is attractive because VOCs can be converted, ideally, to CO2 and H2O at temperatures substantially below those required for thermal incineration. Rare-earth (RE) elements are particularly useful catalyst modifiers because their ionic size, coordination chemistry, redox behavior, oxygen-storage characteristics, and ability to generate lattice defects can be tuned across the lanthanide series. This review critically examines original experimental studies on RE-doped and RE-modified catalysts for thermal, photothermal, photocatalytic, and plasma-assisted VOC degradation, with emphasis on La, Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm, Eu, Gd, Ho, and Y. The evidence shows that RE incorporation can increase oxygen-vacancy concentration, alter the Mn3+/Mn2+ or Ce3+/Ce4+ redox balance, improve lattice-oxygen mobility, modify adsorption strength, stabilize active phases, and enhance resistance to water or chlorine. Representative data include T90 values of 162 °C for Nd-modified Co3O4 during toluene oxidation, 204 °C for CuHoCeOx at high gas hourly space velocity, 202 °C for complete toluene conversion over 1% Sm/CeO2, 255 °C for 4 mol% La-doped CuMnOx, and 120 °C for complete formaldehyde oxidation over 4% Eu/CeO2 nanosheets. However, direct ranking of catalysts is inappropriate unless VOC concentration, space velocity, catalyst loading, oxygen concentration, humidity, reactor configuration, and conversion definition are matched. The review therefore emphasizes structure–property–performance relationships rather than nominal light-off temperatures alone. Remaining challenges include standardization of performance reporting, validation with realistic VOC mixtures, long-term stability under humidity and sulfur/chlorine contaminants, scalable monolith design, and quantitative descriptors linking RE ionic characteristics with oxygen-vacancy formation and reaction kinetics.

W7218557514.title: Rapid Discovery of TiO 2 /ZnFe 2 O 4 /Cu Ternary Photocatalysts for Volatile Organic Compounds Degradation via High‐Throughput Screening Photogenerated Carriers Transfer Properties
W7218557514.abstract: Accelerating the discovery of efficient photocatalysts requires moving beyond conventional trial-and-error experimentation toward rapid and property-guided materials screening. In this work, Tao Liang et al. develop a high-throughput strategy based on photogenerated carrier transport properties to identify TiO2/ZnFe2O4/Cu ternary photocatalysts for VOCs degradation. By combining a composition-gradient thin-film library with micro-area Hall measurements, a promising composition is rapidly identified and validated by photocatalytic toluene degradation. The strong agreement between thin-film and powder-catalyst performance demonstrates the reliability and transferability of this strategy for accelerating multicomponent photocatalyst discovery.

W7214652224.title: Patchy Amorphous TiO2 on Crystalline TiO2 Microspheres with Regulated Surface Hydroxyl Groups for Highly Efficient Photocatalytic Toluene Mineralization
W7214652224.abstract: Abstract Photocatalysis is a promising technology for the removal of volatile organic compounds (VOCs), but achieving complete mineralization of aromatic VOCs remains challenging due to the limited number of active sites and insufficient supply of hydroxyl radicals on the photocatalyst. In this study, we developed a strategy to functionalize crystalline TiO2 microspheres with patchy amorphous TiO2 surface layers, which provided the catalyst with abundant surface hydroxyl groups. Although these groups do not enhance toluene adsorption, they efficiently capture photogenerated charge carriers during the photocatalytic process to produce abundant hydroxyl radicals, which subsequently drive toluene oxidation toward complete mineralization. The optimized photocatalyst demonstrated a toluene degradation efficiency of 100% and a mineralization rate of 94.6%. Combining the results of in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy and theoretical calculations revealed that, compared with pure TiO2, water molecules are more likely to form hydroxyl groups when reaching the surface of amorphous TiO2. Furthermore, under illumination, amorphous TiO2 continuously provides more hydroxyl radicals than pure TiO2 to attack toluene and achieve complete mineralization. This study offers a design prototype for the development of high-performance photocatalysts tailored for VOCs abatement.

W7221064536.title: Dual-site synergistic catalysis on BiOCl: leveraging surface hydroxyl and oxygen vacancies for enhanced photocatalytic mineralization of toluene

W7216206268.title: Preparation of ZSM-5/TiO2 photocatalyst by dip-coating method and evaluation isopropanol removal capacity
W7216206268.journal: Science & Technology Development Journal - Engineering and Technology
W7216206268.abstract: The incorporation of TiO2 with zeolite ZSM-5 has been explored to facilitate photocatalytic activity and establish a continuous volatile organic compound (VOC) treatment system. In this study, composites of ZSM-5 and commercial TiO2 with various ratios were successfully deposited onto cylindrical glass tubes by the dip-coating method using specialized equipment. To improve suspension stability and mitigate the sedimentation of heavy particles, a carboxymethyl cellulose additive was introduced into the mixture. The morphology properties and component determination were characterized with SEM-EDX, revealing the homogeneous distribution after applying the dip-coating method, showing a minor deviation of only 4% to 12% between actual and theoretical mass loadings. Photocatalytic performance was evaluated through the removal of gaseous isopropanol (IPA) utilizing an air simulation system coupled with gas chromatography (GC-FID) analysis. A wide range of factors, including humidity, concentration of VOC, UV light intensity, and the catalyst's mass, were simulated to investigate their effect on the photocatalyst’s performance and make a conclusion in the most optimal working condition. Gas chromatography (GC) analysis of VOC content after treatment asserts the superiority of materials containing ZSM-5 and TiO2 at appropriate ratios (2:8 and 6:4) over TiO2 solely, with higher photocatalytic efficiency (47.7% and 42.9%). The higher the humidity and VOC concentrations, the lower the productivity of the photocatalyst. Furthermore, long-term activity testing demonstrated the excellent structural stability and durability of the optimized composite, which maintained a consistent conversion efficiency of approximately 46% over 6 consecutive hours of continuous operation. Interestingly, doubling the deposited catalyst mass from 0.1 g to 0.2 g yielded no significant increase in photocatalytic efficiency, indicating that performance is primarily governed by the component ratios exposed directly to light rather than total coating mass. Quantitatively, increasing the UV intensity from 2 to 4 lamps significantly accelerated hydroxyl radical generation and doubled the maximum treatment efficiency. Therefore, the most optimal condition and catalyst preparation process should be surveyed for the effectiveness of VOC gas treatment.

W7213401298.title: Loofah-supported Ce-doped ZnO photocatalyst fabricated via plant-mediated synthesis for gas-phase chlorobenzene degradation

W7221554702.title: Catalytic Oxidation of Chlorobenzene: From Mechanistic Insights to the Design of Chlorine-Resistant Catalysts—A Review
W7221554702.abstract: Chlorobenzene (CB), a typical chlorinated volatile organic compound (CVOC), serves as a critical precursor to polychlorinated dibenzo-p-dioxins and dibenzofurans (PCDD/Fs). Efficient catalytic oxidation of CB is vital for air pollution control and solid-waste incineration tail-gas treatment. Based on 123 representative studies, this review addresses five key scientific issues: CB reaction pathways over catalysts and the intrinsic correlation between lattice-oxygen activity and Brønsted acid sites; the nature of active sites (isolated transition-metal centres, interfacial bridges or atomically dispersed noble metals) and the generality of corresponding structure-activity relationships; molecular origins, thermodynamic driving forces and microkinetics of partially reversible chlorine poisoning; effects of real flue-gas components (NOx, toluene, SO2, Hg, etc.) via competitive adsorption, redox disturbance and composite poisoning; and non-thermal-field assistance (plasma, Joule heating, photocatalysis) for overcoming low-temperature activation barriers of thermal catalysis. Assumptions and experimental prerequisites for existing conclusions are highlighted. Critical research gaps are identified in mechanism validation, chlorine mass balance, long-term stability and practical-condition verification. The results indicate that rational design of chlorine-resistant catalysts should not pursue the optimisation of single-performance index, but realise systematic trade-offs among activity, selectivity and durability.

W7214921272.title: Pd0 and oxygen vacancy interfacial synergy regulates charge transfer and oxygen activation for photocatalytic oxidation of gaseous toluene
W7214921272.journal: Colloids and Surfaces A Physicochemical and Engineering Aspects
W7214921272.abstract: The efficient photocatalytic removal of gaseous toluene over TiO 2 is hindered by rapid charge-carrier recombination, inefficient interfacial charge utilization, and limited surface oxygen activation. In this study, Pd nanoparticles and oxygen-vacancy-related defects were simultaneously introduced onto anatase TiO 2 through a one-step NaBH 4 reduction strategy. Pd, TiO 2 , TiO 2-x , and Pd-TiO 2-x were examined to distinguish the respective roles of Pd sites, defect-associated sites, and their coupled interface. Pd-TiO 2-x exhibited an actual Pd loading of 0.948 wt%, with Pd predominantly present in metallic Pd 0 state. Compared with TiO 2-x , Pd-TiO 2-x exhibited a higher concentration of oxygen vacancies and a lower interfacial charge-transfer resistance. Under UV light irradiation, Pd-TiO 2-x achieved a toluene degradation efficiency of 98.62% and a mineralization efficiency of 84.30% after 120 min, with an apparent pseudo-first-order rate constant of 0.06282 min −1 . Notably, despite exhibiting the lowest transient photocurrent among TiO 2 -based catalysts, Pd-TiO 2-x showed the highest photocatalytic activity. This non-parallel behavior suggested that its performance advantage arose primarily from the preferential interfacial migration and reactive utilization of photogenerated charge carriers, rather than from an increase in measurable charge output. Mechanistic analyses indicated that Pd 0 -rich sites promoted electron acceptance and transfer, whereas oxygen-vacancy-related sites facilitated O 2 adsorption and activation, thereby promoting the formation of • O 2 ⁻ and • OH. These results highlighted the reactive utilization of interfacial charges as an important factor governing toluene photocatalytic oxidation.

W7214199431.title: Determinant formation of benzaldehyde-water complexes in the photocatalytic degradation of toluene: An FTIR study
W7214199431.abstract: Studies were conducted on the photocatalytic degradation of toluene and benzaldehyde (BZH) in continuous reactors. These studies were performed in both aerobic and anaerobic conditions. The humidity was kept at saturation levels throughout all experiments, at the laboratory temperature and pressure. FTIR analysis revealed that BZH, the main intermediate in the photocatalytic degradation of toluene, forms a complex with water and TiO 2 . This adsorbed complex gives rise to the geminal diol, which is converted into benzoate in the absence of air, deactivating the catalyst. In contrast, when photocatalytic degradation occurs in humid air, the aforementioned complex evolves as in the previous case to the geminal diol which, in this case, interacts with the adsorbed O 2 molecules, favoring the removal of electrons from the aromatic ring and promoting its rupture by means of photocatalytically generated reactive oxygen species. This process breaks the aromatic ring and forms carboxylic acids that accumulate on the catalyst surface. Depending on their surface area, these accumulated species can partially deactivate the catalysts which can be reactivated by photocatalytic treatment with air. However, the benzoates generated in the absence of air are recalcitrant and cannot be photocatalytically removed in subsequent recovery treatments with illumination and in the presence of air. These studies were conducted with the commercial catalysts P25, P90 and Hombikat UV-100, and a laboratory-synthesized composite called Homb@EST-pH7. The greatest activity under aerobic conditions was observed in catalysts with a higher specific surface area and only anatase phase.

W7214897741.title: Decorating SrTiO 3 With Cu@Pt Core‐Shell Cocatalysts to Promote the Selective Thermally Assisted Photocatalytic Methanol Dehydrogenation to Formaldehyde
W7214897741.abstract: Photocatalytic methanol conversion, a process of particular interest in the context of hydrogen generation, also holds promise as a sustainable approach to chemical synthesis of value‐added products, including formaldehyde. In this study, Cu‐core/Pt‐shell modified SrTiO 3 photocatalysts are demonstrated to enhance the thermally assisted photocatalytic methanol dehydrogenation in the gas phase by 50% compared to Pt/SrTiO 3 photocatalysts prepared by conventional photodeposition, while maintaining a high formaldehyde selectivity. Cu‐core/Pt‐shell structures were prepared by means of galvanic displacement, in which Cu is displaced by Pt, yielding irregular core–shell structures consisting of hexagonal Pt particles. These particles transform during extended operation into smooth core–shell systems, thereby enabling stable methanol dehydrogenation. Initial deactivation of the samples is associated with CO‐induced Pt reconstruction, as evidenced by operando diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy and transmission electron microscopy. Despite this initial deactivation, the photocatalytic performance is found to be attributable to a significantly enhanced charge separation and carrier lifetime. This enhancement is presumed to be the result of the formation of an Ohmic contact between the SrTiO 3 absorber and Cu, thereby, enabling efficient charge transfer to the catalytically active Pt surface. This study underscores the beneficial properties of core–shell cocatalysts and highlights the potential for value‐added chemical production using photocatalysis in the gas phase.

W7221001849.title: Making nitrate and keeping it: selectivity, storage and the back-reaction in photocatalytic NOx abatement

W7214447766.title: Interfacial charge redistribution regulates surface hydroxyl dynamics during photocatalytic nitric oxide oxidation
W7214447766.journal: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science

W7214063412.title: Tailoring TiO2/WO3 composites for high-efficiency NOx abatement: Influence of synthesis method and tungsten source
W7214063412.abstract: The combination of tungsten doping and WO₃ composite formation represents a highly effective approach to enhancing the photocatalytic activity of TiO 2 . The primary objective of this modification is the elimination of NOx air pollutants through the application of a photocatalytic layer. In this study, TiO 2 ‑based composite photocatalysts incorporating both tungsten doping and a WO 3 cocatalyst were synthesized using three distinct methods. The synergistic effect of these two modifications alters the structural and optical properties, alongside the dynamics of photogenerated charge carriers, ultimately resulting in elevated photocatalytic performance. The NOx conversion performance of the prepared photocatalyst composites was investigated under both UV‑A and simulated solar illumination in accordance with the ISO 22197‑1 standard. Under UV‑A irradiation, the TiO 2 /WO 3 physical mixture composite containing 2 wt.% WO 3 exhibited optimal performance, achieving a photocatalytic efficiency of ∼0.29 μmol·m −2 ·mW −1 over 120 minutes. Conversely, under simulated solar irradiation, the highest activity was observed for the TiO 2 prepared by a sol–gel method, which featured simultaneous WO 3 incorporation and tungsten doping utilizing Na 2 WO 4 as the precursor. The measured efficiency for this sample series is one order of magnitude higher than that of the series where H 2 WO 4 was used as the tungsten source, as well as the TiO 2 /WO 3 physical mixture series. With an efficiency of 0.020 μmol·m −2 ·mW −1 , the best member of this series is the composite containing WO 3 at a nominal 10 wt.% (combined WO 3 content and tungsten doping). When converted to realistic environmental parameters, this result corresponds to ∼20.0 mmol·m −2 over 120 minutes.

W7214300603.title: Regulating Proton Supply for Selective Photocatalytic NO Conversion toward Pollutant Removal or Ammonia Recovery
W7214300603.abstract: Abstract Controlling the conversion of nitric oxide (NO) is critical for both air pollution mitigation and nitrogen resource recovery. Proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) governs photocatalytic NO reduction, where reaction pathways determine whether nitrogen is removed as inert N2 or converted into value-added NH3. However, precise control over this selectivity remains challenging, largely due to the limited understanding and regulation of proton delivery. Alcohols with different α-C–H bond strengths are demonstrated to provide tunable proton fluxes. The energetics of α-C–H bonds in alcohol proton donors govern proton delivery and act as a molecular-level regulator for NO removal pathways. Ethanol, which contains a single and relatively inert α-C–H bond, cannot sustain proton delivery and therefore favors N–N coupling, leading to a N2 selectivity of 93.0%. In contrast, ethylene glycol contains two α-C–H positions that adjacent hydroxyl groups activate. As a result, the α-C–H cleavage barrier is lowered, continuous proton release is achieved, and NH3 formation is promoted with a selectivity of 98.3%. Proton generation and pathway selection are determined by α-C–H dehydrogenation, as evidenced by comprehensive mechanistic analyses using isotope-labeled in situ technologies. This work provides a molecular-level strategy for regulating PCET reactions through proton supply modulation, enabling scenario-adapted NO conversion for both pollutant removal and nitrogen resource recovery.

W7219739863.title: Understanding and Steering Nitrogen Fate in Photocatalytic Nitrate Reduction
W7219739863.abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic nitrate reduction is assessed through nitrate conversion, although the reaction can redistribute nitrogen among nitrite, nitric oxide (NO)‐derived intermediates, nitrous oxide (N 2 O), dinitrogen (N 2 ), ammonia/ammonium (NH 3 /NH 4 + ), and emerging C–N products. The environmental and resource value of the process depends on nitrogen fate rather than nitrate disappearance alone. This review establishes a product‐centred framework for understanding and steering that fate. We first consolidate the nitrogen network across surface, liquid, and gas phases, and distinguish primary selectivity from the final product distribution after secondary conversion and phase transfer. We then relate product formation to three coupled levels: nitrate entry, branching of NO‐derived intermediates, and branch completion; surface functions governing adsorption, intermediate binding, cooperative sites, and active hydrogen; and the photochemical redox environment, including charge delivery and the oxidation half‐reaction. Evidence from model systems, real waters, and time‐resolved operation shows why high selectivity under one condition cannot be treated as an intrinsic catalyst property. On this basis, N 2 ‐oriented treatment requires verified removal without nitrite, ammonium, or N 2 O leakage, whereas NH 3 ‐oriented conversion requires product preservation, capture, and a favourable process balance. Connecting working‐interface chemistry with water‐matrix effects, reactor operation, and product recovery provides a route from empirical nitrate removal to deliberate nitrogen management.

W7214395256.title: Development of Multi-functional Nano-Terrazzo Tiles for Educational Facilities: Mechanical Durability, Photocatalytic Activity, and Biological Safety

W7219783178.title: Machine-learning-guided hydrothermal engineering of Cobalt-modified ZnFe₂O₄ for visible-light-active porous photocatalytic coating for urban infrastructure
W7219783178.journal: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A Chemistry
W7219783178.abstract: This study presents a machine-learning-guided hydrothermal strategy for optimizing Cobalt-modified ZnFe 2 O 4 (ZF–Co) photocatalysts. Moreover, a novel scalable porous inorganic coating platform compatible with retrofit implementation on existing urban infrastructures was developed for visible-light-driven atmospheric pollutant mitigation. A hydrothermal synthesis database containing 320 experimentally synthesized ZF–Co samples was generated using temperature (120–250 °C), duration (4–24 h), cobalt concentration (0–20 wt%), and urea-to-metal molar ratio (1.8–9) as input variables, while BET specific surface area (S BET ) was selected as the optimization target. Linear regression, random forest, and XGBoost models were implemented for prediction and optimization. The optimized ZF–Co photocatalyst was subsequently characterized using BET, XRD, FESEM/EDS, TEM/HRTEM, FTIR, and UV–Vis analyses and incorporated into a porous lithium-silicate-based coating containing dispersant and foaming agents. The coating was deposited onto cementitious substrates and evaluated by continuous-flow photocatalytic degradation of NOx, formaldehyde, and toluene under UV-A and visible-light irradiation, along with wettability, compressive strength, and pull-off adhesion tests. XGBoost achieved the highest predictive accuracy with R 2 = 0.947 and RMSE = 4.49 m 2 g −1 , identifying an optimum synthesis condition of ~198 °C, ~6.8 h, ~12.2 wt% Co, and ~2.7 urea-to-metal ratio. Experimental validation yielded a maximum SBET of 126.4 m 2 g −1 with only ~3.0% deviation from the predicted value. The optimized coating achieved ~58% NO conversion and ~42% total NOx removal under UV irradiation, while visible light still provided ~37% and ~28% removal, respectively. Formaldehyde degradation reached ~94% under UV and ~79% under visible light, whereas toluene degradation reached ~61% and ~37%, respectively. The coating additionally exhibited a hydrophobic transition from ~31.6°–33.1° to ~128.4°–129.3°, preserved compressive strength at ~40 MPa, and achieved pull-off adhesion strengths of ~2.1–2.65 MPa. Overall, the results establish a foundation for ML-assisted optimization of ferrite photocatalysts and scalable durable photocatalytic coatings for existing urban infrastructures and diverse construction materials without compromising their intrinsic mechanical functionality or durability. All Python codes and the experimental dataset are provided in the Appendix to ensure reproducibility.

W7214391693.title: Surface Adsorption and ROS Formation in α-Ag2WO4: Linking Theory and Photocatalytic Performance
W7214391693.abstract: Abstract Understanding the relationship between surface structure and photocatalytic performance is essential for the development of semiconductor materials. In this study, hexagonal α-Ag2WO4 rods were investigated using a theoretical-experimental approach, highlighting the influence of surface-dependent reactivity on the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS). Density functional theory calculations showed that the surfaces (001) and (101) favor H2O adsorption and activation to form •OH radicals, while the (010) surface increased O2 adsorption. Furthermore, coadsorption calculations revealed a synergistic interaction between H2O and O2, which favors ROS generation. The experimental data obtained for α-Ag2WO4 samples synthesized via a coprecipitation route in water, ammonia, and ethanol as solvents indicate the ability to tune defect and morphology without affecting its hexagonal structure. The highest crystallinity and anisotropy were observed for the samples synthesized in water. On the other hand, synthesis in ethanol yields higher defect densities and sub-coordinated silver quantum cluster-rich surfaces. The photocatalytic activity was evaluated considering rhodamine B under UV light, with and without air bubbling. The samples synthesized in aqueous medium exhibited enhanced response (approximately 76% removal), which can be ascribed to the greater reactivity of (001)/(101) exposed surfaces, and •OH radical generation, whose presence was confirmed by coumarin probes and scavenger tests. Under bubbling conditions, the sample synthesized in an ethanolic medium exhibited complete dye degradationover 10 times faster compared to samples synthesized in waterwhich may be related to O2 reduction activation pathways rather than H2O-based mechanisms. DMA probing experiments and scavengers’ tests revealed higher •O2− and 1O2 generation under O2-rich conditions, suggesting a higher availability of active sites for the reduction of oxygen into ROS species as a result of the defect-rich samples synthesized in ethanol. This work provides a practical strategy for tailoring α-Ag2WO4 particle morphologyengineering surfaces and controlling exposed facetsenabling selective ROS formation for enhanced photocatalytic response, which is essential for the rational development of advanced semiconductor photocatalysts.

W7219083812.title: Donor-acceptor conjugated organic polymers for light-driven durable and direct air-to-nitric acid conversion
W7219083812.abstract: The production of nitric acid directly from ambient air offers a promising pathway for ammonia-free synthesis of this essential chemical. Herein, we report a donor-acceptor conjugated porous organic polymer that enables durable and direct photosynthesis of nitric acid from air at room temperature. Remarkably, the polymer maintains high catalytic activity even after 324 h of light irradiation, achieving a substantial nitric acid yield up to 4466.2 μmol·g⁻ 1 cat . The reaction mechanism underlying the photocatalytic nitric acid synthesis is systematically investigated through a combination of experimental studies and theoretical calculations. Additionally, the reaction intermediates are monitored by NMR, EPR, MS and DRIFTS. Based on the results, a reaction pathway involving O 2 reduction, in situ •OH generation and N 2 oxidation at the acceptor site of the polymer is proposed. This work presents a metal-free photocatalytic process for the direct synthesis of nitric acid from air under mild conditions.

W7215122363.title: Global prospects of low-carbon photocatalytic hydrogen based on regionalised optimisation
W7215122363.abstract: Photocatalytic hydrogen has gained interest as a solar-driven pathway for renewable hydrogen production, particularly in regions with abundant sunlight and remote locations with limited industrial infrastructure. However, its large-scale potential and environmental performance remain unexplored. This study aims to estimate the global production potential of photocatalytic hydrogen under realistic environmental, technological and land-use constraints based on a representative system, and to assess its prospective carbon footprint in 2050. A bottom-up, regionalised optimisation framework was developed by coupling an experimental kinetic model with global datasets of direct normal irradiance and air temperature (11,301 points worldwide). The photocatalytic hydrogen carbon footprint was optimised for each location. Land-use filtering was applied to retain only degraded and desert soils outside key biodiversity areas. Results show that the global production potential reaches 4.58 Mt H 2 per year, associated with a carbon footprint of 10.27 Mt CO 2 eq per year. Although this production potential represents 1.31% of the projected 2050 hydrogen demand, these greenhouse gas emissions correspond to 0.15% of the global climate change carrying capacity, emphasising the need to contextualise performance relative to environmental thresholds. Overall, the results identify the locations where photocatalytic hydrogen could become feasible under future conditions, while showing that its global production contribution remains conditioned by further improvements in catalyst performance, key material carbon footprints, and light-to-fuel conversion.

W7221772102.title: Solar-driven photocatalytic air purification for road infrastructure: Pollutant dynamics, material integration, and sustainable engineering
W7221772102.abstract: Road infrastructure provides a scalable platform for integrating photocatalytic technologies to mitigate urban air pollution. However, practical deployment remains uncertain because pollutants in road environments show substantial diversity and dynamic variation in their emission sources, exposure levels, and catalytic degradation processes. Although advances in materials science continue to expand the range and performance of photocatalysts, field applications remain constrained by insufficient solar energy utilization, mass transfer limitations, environmental durability, and selective pollutant conversion. This review establishes a framework linking target pollutants with photocatalytic application strategies in road infrastructure. It identifies low-concentration nitrogen oxides (NOx) and volatile organic compounds (VOCs), together with particulate matter (PM) associated with the secondary atmospheric transformation of these gaseous precursors, as key future targets for road air pollution control. The overall pathway through which photocatalysis reduces exposure to gaseous precursors and improves ambient air quality is further clarified. Progress across four representative engineering platforms is critically assessed, including cement concrete, asphalt pavements, aggregates, and roadside air purification installations. Different application strategies differ in catalyst immobilization, gas phase exposure, and environmental adaptability, and adopt distinct pathways for performance optimization. Understanding light response, charge separation, and interactions with engineering matrices provides a mechanistic basis for interpreting performance in engineering applications, including degradation efficiency, selectivity, durability, and feasibility. The review further identifies key challenges and future directions and highlights emerging opportunities in energy harvesting, multi field coupled catalysis, low carbon design, high value utilization of solid waste, multifunctionality, and long term durability.

W7221990327.title: Fumigation, Gaseous Decontamination, and No-Touch Environmental Technologies in the Operating Theatre: A Narrative Review
W7221990327.abstract: Background: Environmental decontamination is essential for infection prevention in operating theatres (OTs), yet terminology, evidence and implementation practices vary considerably. Objective: To review the efficacy, safety and implementation of traditional fumigation and contemporary no-touch decontamination technologies. Methods: A structured narrative search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Google Scholar prioritised systematic reviews and OT-specific studies. Formal risk-of-bias and GRADE assessments were not performed. Results: Formaldehyde demonstrates broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity but presents substantial occupational health risks and prolonged environmental persistence. Vaporized hydrogen peroxide and aerosolized hydrogen peroxide are distinct technologies, with vaporized hydrogen peroxide having the strongest evidence base among gaseous approaches, although clinical findings remain variable. Ozone and chlorine dioxide demonstrate antimicrobial efficacy under laboratory conditions, but clinical evidence is limited and stringent safety measures are required. Ultraviolet-C has moderate supporting evidence as an adjunct to manual cleaning. Plasma air treatment and far-UVC require further evaluation, while photocatalytic coatings remain investigational. Clinical trials have not established a clear benefit for plasma air treatment. Conclusion: No single technology suits all OT settings. Selection should consider efficacy, safety, cost and institutional capacity, with manual cleaning remaining fundamental and automated technologies serving as adjuncts. Keywords: Fumigation, Operating Rooms, Communicable Disease Control, Hydrogen Peroxide, Decontamination, Ultraviolet Rays, Review

W7222551833.title: Stable Nitrogen-Doped TiO2 Sols with Enhanced Visible-Light Response and Surface Wettability for Air Purification
W7222551833.abstract: Photocatalytic coatings that can be immobilized on outdoor surfaces provide a promising route for distributed and passive purification of atmospheric pollutants. The practical application requires not only visible-light photocatalytic activity but also stable dispersion, facile coating and favorable interfacial properties. In this work, N-doped TiO2 (N-TiO2) sols with different nominal doping contents were prepared through hydrothermal treatment of peroxotitanic acid precursors containing different amounts of urea at 130 °C for 4 h. All samples exhibited anatase phase, while the shifts in XRD and Raman peaks indicated nitrogen-doping-induced lattice distortion. The sols exhibited monomodal particle size distributions with average hydrodynamic diameters in the range of 20.13 nm to 27.07 nm, and the high absolute zeta potentials (>30 mV) demonstrated good dispersion stability. The XPS results confirmed that nitrogen atoms were introduced at interstitial sites with Ti-O-N bonds and increased the relative proportion of surface hydroxyl oxygen from 13.9% to 34.2%. Nitrogen doping improved the visible-light absorption by decreasing the bandgap from 3.06 eV to 2.81 eV and reduced the water contact angle of the sol-derived films from 24.0° to as low as 8.6°. Among all samples, 1.0N-TiO2 exhibited the highest NO removal efficiency of 72.5% under visible-light irradiation and retained good stability over five photocatalytic cycles. These results demonstrate that moderate nitrogen doping can simultaneously regulate the colloidal, optical and interfacial properties of TiO2 sols, making them promising coating materials for functionalization of building envelopes or other outdoor surfaces for air purification.

W7222597305.title: Chain-length-dependent structure–activity relationships in the deep oxidation of multi-component aldehydes over an S-scheme ternary bismuth oxynitride/titanium dioxide/graphite heterojunction photocatalyst
W7222597305.abstract: Photocatalytic oxidation (PCO) offers a scalable route for indoor aldehyde abatement, yet practical deployment is hindered by potential surface deactivation from competitive adsorption and accumulation of oxygenated intermediates under realistic multi-component and humidified conditions. Here, a series of ternary heterojunctions, comprising bismuth oxynitride (Bi 5 O 7 NO 3 : BN), titanium dioxide (TiO 2 : T), and graphite (G) (denoted as TGBN-x, “x” = BN/TG wt%), are immobilized on honeycomb cordierite and integrated into a portable air purifier (AP) device. In a 23-L closed-loop chamber, these AP-PCO systems are evaluated for abatement of single- and mixed-aldehydes [formaldehyde (FA), acetaldehyde (AA), propionaldehyde (PA), and valeraldehyde (VA)] under varying operating conditions. Under dry conditions, the optimized TGBN-10 filter records 100% FA (5 ppm) removal within 6 min of 1 W UV-LED illumination, while doubling the catalyst loading from 0.05 to 0.1 g enhances the chamber clean air delivery rate (CADR) from 8.3 to 16.0 L min − 1 . It also exhibits superior charge-carrier dynamics (relative to binary and single counterpart catalysts), delivering an 8.93-fold higher specific CADR (SCADR) at 5 ppm FA (near-ambient level) than at 100 ppm (industrially-relevant level), and a 1.70-fold higher SCADR than the binary TG composite under identical conditions. At 100 ppm FA (100 ppm per aldehyde in the mixture), its SCADR increases 2.64-fold (from 7 to 18.51 L min − 1 g − 1 ) when the inlet gas-phase shifts from a multi-component to a single-component system, underscoring the strong dependence of PCO performance on both inlet concentration and gas-phase composition. In a multi-component mixture (total C 0 = 100 ppm), the peak PCO reaches 91% for FA, compared with 23.2% (PA), 60.7% (VA), and 5.8% (AA), while the overall CO 2 yield across all aldehydes attains 95.9%, confirming a deep mineralization pathway. In situ DRIFTS measurements reveal hydroxyl-mediated FA activation via dioxymethylene and formate intermediates, with carboxylate accumulation increasing from valerate to acetate. It also sustains high PCO activity over 5 cycles and UV-driven photo-regeneration in clean air, with minimal activity loss due to reversible carbonaceous fouling rather than structural degradation. Combined photoelectrochemical, EPR, DRIFTS, and XPS findings further support S-scheme-like charge separation in TGBN-10, with graphite likely serving as a conductive interfacial mediator. These findings demonstrate the potential of TGBN-10 as a functional noble-metal-free photocatalyst for aldehyde VOC abatement under representative industrial/indoor-air conditions.

W7222829459.title: Enhanced Photocatalytic Activity of Titania Nanosheets via Morphology Control and Interface Engineering
W7222829459.abstract: Abstract The photocatalytic oxidation of volatile organic compounds over titania nanosheets represents a promising strategy for efficient pollutant removal; however, the effects of nanosheet morphology and interface engineering on photocatalytic activity and selectivity remain insufficiently understood. In this study, titania nanosheets of a crystallographic thickness of 0.75 nm were assembled into molecularly thin monolayer films, and the photocatalytic oxidation of 2-propanol under UV irradiation was systematically examined using films with controlled nanosheet dimensions, different substrate electrical properties, and sectioned nanosheets. The initial reaction rate increased with increasing nanosheet size, whereas nanosheets with lateral dimensions of 3−6 μm exhibited the highest long-term photocatalytic activity. Increasing substrate resistivity enhanced the reaction rate but simultaneously brought about a shift in the product selectivity toward partially oxidized intermediates such as acetone. Further enhancement of the photocatalytic performance was achieved through nanosheet sectioning, which is attributed to the generation of edges exposing well-defined crystallographic facets. In addition, heterostructured bilayer films were designed by assembling a monolayer film of zeolite nanosheets onto a monolayer film of titania nanosheets, and their photocatalytic properties were examined. Although the intrinsic oxidation reactivity of the monolayer titania nanosheet film followed the order 2-propanol > ethanol > methanol, consistent with the relative stability of the intermediate radicals, deposition of a microporous MFI zeolite nanosheet overlayer decreased the overall conversion because of diffusional limitations, with the extent of conversion suppression depending on the kinetic diameter of the reactant. In particular, the conversion of larger alcohols was substantially suppressed, whereas that of methanol remained essentially unchanged, indicating that the MFI overlayer modulates the accessibility of reactants to the photocatalytically active surface. These findings demonstrate that both the activity and selectivity of titania nanosheet photocatalysts can be rationally tailored through control of the nanosheet morphology, substrate properties, and integration with a microporous overlayer.

W7222953667.title: A Thermophilic Bacteriophage TP-84 Surrogate System for Validating Photocatalytic and Ultraviolet Inactivation of Airborne Viruses, Including SARS-CoV-2
W7222953667.abstract: The airborne transmission of SARS-CoV-2 has renewed interest in engineering controls for indoor air; photocatalytic oxidation over titanium dioxide (TiO2) under ultraviolet (UV) light is an attractive, reagent-free basis for such controls. Rational development requires a biosafe, quantifiable challenge organism usable at biosafety level 1 (BSL-1). We validated the thermophilic bacteriophage TP-84 (host Geobacillus stearothermophilus) as a surrogate for airborne viruses, characterising its stability, aerosolisation, recovery from photocatalytic supports and inactivation on TiO2 surfaces under UVA, UVC and UVA + UVC by a reference-normalised mass balance. TP-84 was stable in a simulated saliva matrix, survived ultrasonic nebulisation, and was recovered from porous ceramic supports at 66.0–91.7%. Five minutes of UV on TiO2 surfaces—UVC (254 nm, 540 mJ cm−2) or combined UVA + UVC (2040 mJ cm−2)—inactivated 87.4–89.4% and 61.6–76.5% of phage, respectively; bulk liquid was strongly protective (94.6–97.5% recovery), whereas desiccation reduced recovery to 4.3–16%. Flow-through aerosol assays provided a device test bed. Because TP-84 is a hardy, non-enveloped dsDNA virus, these values are conservative lower bounds that must not be equated with SARS-CoV-2 efficacy; validation with an enveloped surrogate and authentic virus is the next step.

W7222956001.title: Integrated Solar Photovoltaic and Water Purification Systems for Rural Tanzania: A Review of Technologies and Deployment Barriers
W7222956001.abstract: In rural Tanzania, unreliable electricity constrains decentralized water treatment. This review evaluates Photovoltaic (PV) powered ultraviolet (UV) disinfection and reverse osmosis/nanofiltration (RO/NF), chlorination, filtration and photocatalysis. A structured narrative search of one engineering database (ScienceDirect) and one academic search engine (Google Scholar) covered 2016–2026. The cited evidence base comprised 45 publications from 2016–2026, three earlier foundational sources and five institutional/report sources (53 sources total). Tanzanian Photovoltaic (PV) powered ultrafiltration–nanofiltration (UF–NF) field tests produced about 1,200 L per solar day at approximately 1.5 kWh/m³; auxiliary air bubbling could add about 0.8 kWh/m³. Tanzania receives about 4–7 kWh/m²/day of solar irradiation, but rainy-season cloud cover can reduce PV output when treatment demand may rise. Filtration plus chlorination is the most deployable near-term pathway. The proposed decision framework integrates source-water type, specific energy consumption (SEC), solar/grid reliability, operator capacity, supply chain and maintenance.
